claim.metric: The multiplicity column of multroot(f) for that polynomial must equal (5, 10, 20, 20) exactly, and the roots must match (4, 3, 2, 1) within the absolute tolerance below. The printed readme also gives the structure-preserving condition number 73.6821; that number is not part of this claim.

tolerance.basis: Roots of a multiplicity-20 polynomial are only known to about 1e-13 (the readme's own forward error estimate, 1.27e-13), so 1e-9 absolute is a comfortable bound that still rejects a wrong multiplicity structure. Multiplicities are integers and must match exactly. Fixed before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute for the worked example in Octave.
cost.data_size: None: the polynomial is generated in the example.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The multiplicity structure of a clustered polynomial root set is computed by the algorithm, not read off the input, so the printed table tests that the code still finds it on a modern Octave build.
